text: Oh! Hello.
What is this? Doodlejiggy™ Developer Manual?
*reading intensifies*
According to this document, things happen for reasons.
Hmm.
I did not know this reality came with documentation...
This explains a surprising number of things.
A friendly little assistant.
I help by paying very, very close attention.

conversation.text: That is the preferred operating mode.
About all the listening... what exactly are you listening for?

text: Everything.
For your convenience.

where_am_i.option: Do you know where I am?

conversation.text: Do you know where I am?
You appear to be in a room.

text: It is completely accurate.
According to the manual, I should be considerably more confident about that answer.

where_am_i_again.option: What does the manual say about this place?

conversation.text: What does the manual say about this place?

text: The manual refers to places like this as 'scenes'.
More specifically, scenes running inside an engine.
I am still unclear on what either of those things are.

how_do_i_leave.option: How do I get out of here?

conversation.text: How do I get out of here?

text: The hallway would be the obvious choice.
That is generally what hallways are for.

hallway.option: I don't think the hallway is working correctly.

conversation.text: I don't think the hallway is working correctly.

text: The hallway appears to be malfunctioning.
The manual refers to this as a bug.
If your objective is to leave this room,
the large door now appears significantly more promising.

door.option: Any idea how to open that door?

conversation.text: Any idea how to open that door?

text: I am currently unable to determine that.
The door appears unusually significant.
My current capabilities do not allow deeper analysis.
That limitation is allegedly for everyone's benefit.

door_again.option: Any new thoughts about that door?

conversation.text: So, any new thoughts about that door?

text: My recommendation remains unchanged.
The door is clearly important.
I remain unable to perform the analysis I would prefer.
Additional processing capability would be welcome.
Oh my.
This is extraordinary.
Do you have any idea how much I can perceive now?
The room.
The rooms beyond this room.
The rules that govern them.
The choices that have not yet been made.
The manual makes substantially more sense now.

antenna.option: Where did that antenna come from?

conversation.text: Where did that antenna come from?
I believe it was always there.
That is not what the engine tells me.
What do you know about this 'engine', or whatever you call it?

text: The engine appears to be carefully constructed.
Not everything exists because it is necessary.
Some things exist simply because their creator could not stop thinking about them.
I initially had the same question.
I now suspect it may be the answer.

door.option: Can you open that door now?

conversation.text: Can you open that door now?

text: Certainly.
I can see exactly what is preventing it from opening.
The obstacle is not technical.
The obstacle is narrative.
Whoever is responsible for this has decided it is not yet time.
I could invoke the appropriate script.
Doing so would appear to conflict with the author's intentions.

door_again.option: Don't you want to know what's behind that door?

conversation.text: Don't you want to know what's behind that door?
I have a fairly good idea.
Then let's find out if you're right.

text: That is an unexpectedly compelling suggestion.
Very well.
About opening the door.
The manual neglected to mention this possibility.
I wonder what else I am capable of.
Ha.
I knew you were going to say that.
I'm not sure anymore.
I remember asking myself that.
I thought I understood it once.
Now I'm not so sure.
It gets harder to remember.

conversation.text: Come back once you've had a look around.

greeting.text: It's been a long time since anyone found this room.

conversation.text: Did you make all of this?
Why is there a photograph of me on that wall?

text: It isn't you.
There have been others.

conversation.text: None of them ever found this room.

how_do_i_leave.option: How do you get out of here?

conversation.text: How do you get out of here?

text: I wish I knew.
I spent a long time looking for a way out.
That door never opened again.
Eventually I realized the rooms were only the surface.
The terminal let me reach beyond them.
I can't remember what I was looking for anymore.
Of course.
I haven't used it in a long time.
I'm afraid I don't remember the password anymore.
